title: The Sh2-284 nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
caption: The Sh2-284 nebula, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: Sh2-284 · constellation Monoceros · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Bright orange and red colors fill this detailed view of the Sh2-284 nebula, captured by the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile.

Sh2-284 is a star formation region. At its center lies a cluster of young stars nicknamed Dolidze 25, and that cluster is the source of the colors. Its radiation is strong enough to ionize the hydrogen gas in the nebula's cloud, stripping electrons from the atoms. As the atoms recapture electrons, the gas glows, and it is this process that produces the bright orange and red hues.

The picture belongs to a much larger effort, a VST survey that measures hydrogen-alpha light across the southern plane and bulge of our galaxy, headed by Janet Drew of the UK's University of Hertfordshire. Surveys like this one map large stretches of the Milky Way in the light of glowing hydrogen, which makes them good at finding star-forming regions such as Sh2-284. The image also includes ultraviolet and near-infrared filters.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (45.00 x 45.00 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 196 × 196 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope, using near-ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The caption says the orange and red come from ionized hydrogen, but the full filter-to-color mapping is not published.
